subject.title: WhatsApp 1:1: inbound image wedges main lane ~3min before processing — multimodal run strands active_reply_work/queued_work_without_active_run (repro on 2026.6.10, post-#95039)

question: Should OpenClaw release stale active reply work immediately when queued WhatsApp/session work is behind terminal run progress, or keep the current stale-threshold protection and fix only the proven owner/pump leaks?
rationale: The remaining choice changes session recovery semantics: early release reduces user-visible message stalls, while threshold-gated release protects valid active embedded runs from being aborted.

options.title: Keep focused and decide with live proof
options.body: Keep this issue open, collect current-main WhatsApp direct proof, then land a focused recovery policy fix that preserves fresh-work guards.

options.title: Fold into the broad tracker
options.body: Close this as duplicate only if maintainers want all remaining active_reply_work semantics handled under https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/76038 or https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/97538.

options.title: Accept threshold recovery
options.body: Treat the current stale-threshold recovery as intended only after live current-main evidence shows the 24-26 minute loop is gone.

recommendation.title: Keep focused and decide with live proof
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open, collect current-main WhatsApp direct proof, then land a focused recovery policy fix that preserves fresh-work guards.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the related dormant follow-up drain fix and has the strongest visible history on queue/recovery policy tradeoffs.
